key_insight: The paper proposes an ancilla-free, resource-efficient way to simulate Lindbladian open-system dynamics on NISQ hardware by combining a compact mixed-unitary channel with adaptive variational trajectory compression.
engineering_relevance: It reduces circuit depth and qubit overhead for dissipative quantum simulation, making near-term implementation of open quantum system models more practical.
method: Approximate Pauli dissipation with a stable mixed-unitary adjoint channel and sample trajectories without ancilla qubits.
Train a depth-adaptive variational quantum circuit to compress repeated Trotterized Hamiltonian segments.
Replace repeated unitary blocks in sampled trajectories with the trained compressed circuits to lower depth.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical simulations on the dissipative quantum XY model, showing the method is accurate and resource efficient.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of variational training and the approximation error introduced by replacing exact repeated unitary segments.
paper_title: Simulation of Lindbladian dynamics via adaptive variational quantum trajectory compression
